input.quote: 13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
input.rationale: Section 13 binds Clear Capital as well as RadialSpark. It already meets most of the fallback: it is mutual, limited to personnel with direct involvement in the Services, runs only for the term plus one year, and is a solicitation restriction rather than a no-hire. However, it contains no carve-out for general advertisements/untargeted recruiting or for unsolicited approaches, which the rule treats as a required element of an acceptable non-solicit ("narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out"). Without it, ordinary hiring activity could breach the clause. The redline adds only the carve-out sentence, leaving duration and scope untouched, which brings the clause to the fallback position.

proposal.summary: Add general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs to the mutual non-solicit.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added the customary carve-outs so that general advertising and unsolicited approaches by personnel do not breach the non-solicit; our playbook accepts a narrow, time-limited mutual non-solicit only with these exclusions. The mutual scope and one-year duration are otherwise acceptable to us.

ops.oldText: which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
ops.newText: which shall not be unreasonably withheld. This Section shall not restrict either party from (a) placing general advertisements or conducting other recruiting efforts not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, or hiring any person who responds thereto, or (b) hiring any person who approaches such party on an unsolicited basis.
